title.narrative: Hands Off NSA

description.narrative:
Brief overall description: North Star Alliance provides health services to sex workers at Road Wellness Clinics along the transport corridor. Under Hands Off North Star Alliance will continue to increase access to sex workers and build an inclusive, health-literate sex worker community. Peer educators will mobilise their peers to visit the clinic, and work with nurses to stimulate sex workers to make safe and healthy choices. Influential community member gathered in Crisis Response Teams will work to reduce stigma from the community and provide support to sex workers who experienced violence.
Description of objectives: Hands Off II partners work to reduce violence against sex workers at community, national and regional level. Outcomes of North Star Alliance include increased access to and use of services for sex workers, as well as a more enabling environment for sex work.
Description of target groups: The programme’s primary target group is female, male and transgender sex workers, meaning those who receive money or goods in exchange for sexual services, either regularly or occasionally. North Star Alliance also works with influential community leaders.
Additional information (if available): Structural barriers such as stigma, discrimination and criminalisation hinder sex workers to access comprehensive rights based services. In many cases sex workers rely on public health services, however these are often inaccessible for sex workers located outside of the urban areas.

description.narrative: Number of sex workers reached by communities and networks with information on their rights

comment.narrative: A total number of 39 female SWs 24 years and younger were reached with information on their rights. Due to the involvement of community gatekeepers we are at 87% of last year's annual reach. We are making increased progress with this population and are confident we will be able to progressively increase our annual reach. A total number of 118 female SWs 25 years and older were reached with information on their rights. Progress dipped as we progressed through COVID however we are working on increasing our reach - this first half of 2022 has progressed well. We are still working towards reaching almost 2000 clients by the end of the project. A total number of 2 male SWs 24 years and younger were reached with information on their rights. Progress on this indicator is particularly slow and will be a priority for the second half of 2022. A total number of 17 male SWs 25 years and older were reached with information on their rights. This indicator is progressing well with the overall progress at 53%. We require 47 clients to reach the target which we are confident we can achieve by the end of the project. It is also great to see the overall increase from year to year for this indicator. A total number of 3 transgender SWs 24 years and younger were reached with information on their rights. Once againg the progress on this indicator is slow because these clients remain hard to reach. We are encouraged to have the highest reach for the last 6 months and building on this we believe we can progressively increase our reach on providing clients with information on their rights. A total number of 11 transgender SWs 25 years and older were reached with information on their rights. This indicator has progressed well from last year with us doubling last year's annual reach in just 6 months. We are confident we can build on this progress for the remainder of the project.

From North Star: We conducted several Sexual Health Rigths and Safety Training workshops in the 2nd half of the year. Through the CRT meetings, our stakeholders are more invloved and champions our project among the SW's. We have several SW's that participate in the CRT meetings, and therefore are champions in the communities where our sites are. We have established new relationships towards the latter part of the year with rigths groups.

title.narrative: Number of sex workers reached by communities and networks with SRHR and HIV/AIDS information

description.narrative: Number of sex workers reached by communities and networks with SRHR and HIV/AIDS information

comment.narrative: A total of 410 SWs 24 years and younger were reached with SRHR and HIV/AIDS information. During the first half of this year. Noting that this is a biannual indicator report efforts are being made to ensure we reach the additional 1240 needed to reach the target. A total number of 1774 female SWs 25 years and older were reached with SRHR and HIV/AIDS information. Currently we have reached 61% of the overall project target. North Star is working to scale up overall reach to ensure reaching the remaining 6813 SWs needed to reach the target which we are well on our way to reaching. A total number of 6 male SWs 24 years and younger were reached during the first half of 2022. This improvement is based on the Survey conducted with the aim of identifying the specific health needs of LGBTQI SWs. This remains a hard to reach population that North Star is committed to reaching. Currently we require 30 additional clients to be reached and as services have recovered from COVID we are well on our way to reaching the project target with current performance at 70% already. A total number of 13 male SWs 25 years and older have been reached with SRHR and HIV/AIDS information. Our current performance for the overall project is at 64%. Currently we need to reach 36 clients to ensure meeting the project target. North Star is making good progress with this population group and is well on its way to reaching the overall target. A total number of 2 transgender SWs 24 years and younger were reached with information on SRHR and HIV/AIDS. Once again this is a particularly hard to reach population however with the recent survey to better understand the needs of LGBTQI SWs we are confident our reach will increase in the coming months. This indicator performance is currently only at 18% with a reach of 41 still needed to reach the target. A total number of 18 transgender SWs 25 years and older were reached during the first half of 2022 with information on HIV/AIDS and SRHR. North Star's reach to this particular population group has increased progressively over the last 3 years with our current progress at 54%. We are well on our way to reaching and possibly exceeding the target for this indicator.

comment.narrative: A total number of 13 female SWs 24 years and younger accessed legal support services. A collaborative approach through the CRT enabled us to more than a 118% increase in reach compared to last year. A total number of 45 female SWs 25 years and older accessed accessed legal support services. This indicator has been informed by the data available in ONA and the overall progress for this year looks positive. There is an increasing need for legal support across sex workers. A total number of 1 male SWs 24 years and younger accessed accessed legal support services. There is a need to further educate this population on their rights and improve their access to these valuable services. A total number of 1 male SWs 25 years and older accessed accessed legal support services. Consistent with the other male indicator for legal services, there is a need to further educate this population on their rights and increase their access to services. No transgender SWs under the age of 24 years access legal support. North Star is committed to ensuring that those clients who need legal services have equal access to them. A total number of 1 transgender SWs 25 years and older accessed accessed legal support services. Although limited progress we are committed to increasing the overall access to legal services amongst this population group.

title.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

description.narrative: Number of sex workers accessing community-led support after violence

comment.narrative: A total number of 16 female SWs 24 years and younger accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. This has been made possible through the religious leaders who are CRT members. Progress over the years has been relatively consistent however we are committed to increasing our progress to ensure young female SWs are able and free to access community-led support after violent incidents. A total number of 54 female SWs 25 years and older accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. We are making progress with this indicator although it is slow and has remained somewhat consistent over the last 2 years. We are committed to ensuring increased progress on this indicator. A total number of 1 male SWs 24 years and younger accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. This indicator is low especially because males don’t like to admit they have been subject to a violent incident. We are working to help change this perception and behaviour - we want to see young men be able to access support for violence. It may be worth considering a realignment of this target to the same as the below indicator knowing that our reach in this age group is normally lower than the older age group. A total number of 3 male SWs 25 years and older accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. We are making progress with this indicator although it is very slow and mostly influenced by cultural perceptions and behaviour. A total number of 2 transgender SWs 24 years and younger accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. This indicator was doubled from the previous 2 years however it still remains low. We are working on trying to break the barriers that prevent transgender clients from accessing support after violence. A total number of 2 transgender SWs 25 years and older accessed community-led support after experiencing violence. We are making progress with this indicator with current performance at 35%.

Many males refuse to report GBVs, fear of further stigmatisation and being laughed at. From the recent reflections meetings which were attended by some Transgender, they expressed their fear to do so. We are working with them as well as the victim friendly police to show more empathy and not laugh at them.

comment.narrative: A total number of 659 female SWs 24 years and younger accessed health and testing services. In order for us to continue to progress on this indicator we will increase our outreach activities. Currently we are at 77% of the project target which we are confident we will meet by the end of the project. A total number of 3157 female SWs 25 years and older accessed health and testing services. Clients who tested for HIV (a total of 241), 20% of these tested positive for HIV. Currently we are performing well on this indicator and are confident we will reach the target by the end of the project. A total number of 6 male SWs 24 years and younger accessed health and testing services. We are progressing well with this indicator with overall progress at 70% however more effort will be dedicated to increasing our annual number of clients accessing services. A total number of 3 male SWs 25 years and older accessed health and testing services. This indicator has progressed well over the years of implementation and is currently sitting on 88%. We are confident we will be able to reach the target before the end of the project. A total number of 2 transgender SWs 24 years and younger accessed health and testing services. This indicator is progressing slowly and we are committed to increasing this client category's access to health and testing services. Once again clients need to disclose this information which can sometimes be a sensitive topic especially in some cultures and communities. A total number of 1 transgender SWs 25 years and older accessed health and testing services. This indicator is progressing particularly slowly because we have a small pool of transgender SWs that we are working with at the moment - or rather who have disclosed their status.
